clue.text: After study, the battle's course is clear

indicators.note: after says the river piece follows straight on from the study piece

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
the Somme is the river along whose course the 1916 battle was fought

explanation.surface: Once the matter has been studied, the direction the battle will take is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' looks like the definition (a course of a meal) and 'clear' an adjective, but 'the battle's course' is the river SOMME and 'clear' is the noun, as in a clear soup.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear is a thin, transparent soup, and a consommé is exactly that kind of broth.

clue.text: Modest husband finds place in Indian social system

indicators.note: finds place in says the husband letter is set inside the system

parts.note: the caste system is the traditional Hindu social hierarchy

explanation.surface: A demure husband settles into his place in Indian society.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained in conduct, which is close to modest or decorous.

clue.text: Rabbit Jack could turn into a toad

definitions.text: Jack could turn into a toad

explanation.surface: A rabbit called Jack, who might be magically changed into a toad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is British slang for chatter; and adding JACK makes the natterjack, a European toad.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit on is to chatter, as is to natter; with Jack after it the word names a European toad species.

clue.text: Description of human thumb is open to contradiction

explanation.surface: Describing the human thumb is a matter some people dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumb that can meet the other fingers is so described; and an argument that can be disputed or countered is also so described.

clue.text: Accidental death coming between the motorways and the river

indicators.note: between says the arrival word sits in the middle of the motorways and the river

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway, so several of them are M1s, read as MIS
an advent is a coming or arrival
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone was killed on a stretch of road between the motorway and the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the London-Leeds motorway; the digit 1 is read as the letter I. A British inquest records 'death by misadventure' for an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Misadventure is the legal verdict for an accidental death with no crime involved.

clue.text: Get down fluid to the limit

parts.note: an edge is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: Drink something right to the last drop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' reads as swallowing, but here it means to grow downy feathers, as a young bird does.
explanation.definitionFit: A nestling acquires its first soft plumage, its down, when it fledges.

clue.text: No support for the leg in this dance!

indicators.note: support for says the nought sits under the limb, holding it up in a down entry

parts.note: a leg is a limb
O, nought, means none

explanation.surface: You get nothing to hold your leg up in this kind of dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance has a dancer leaning backwards under a low bar with nothing to support them.
explanation.definitionFit: The limbo is a West Indian dance in which the dancer bends back to pass under a bar.

clue.text: Draw out angle exceptionally small

indicators.note: out means the letters of draw are put out of place and rearranged

parts.note: to angle is to fish with a rod and line

explanation.surface: Extend an angle that is especially tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw out angle' reads as geometry; 'out' rearranges DRAW into DWAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfish means stunted, abnormally undersized.

clue.text: All enthusiastic at first, and in the fullest sense united

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of enthusiastic

parts.note: very can mean real or utter, the thing in the fullest sense
one means united, as in at one

explanation.surface: Everybody keen from the start and wholly together.
explanation.definitionFit: All people taken together is the same as every single person.

clue.text: Take not a step out of line, before the numbers are known

indicators.note: out of line says the letters of not a step stand in disorder and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to keep in step, not stray from the ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: In British horse-race betting, an ante-post bet is placed before the runners' numbers are posted on the board on race day.
explanation.definitionFit: Ante-post wagers are struck in advance, ahead of the day's runners being declared and numbered.

clue.text: Spit in beer — the little devil started it

indicators.note: started it says the devil comes first, ahead of the beer

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Someone spat in a drink, and the little rascal was the one who began it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit' looks like spitting into a drink, but it is the verb meaning to skewer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spit something is to run a pointed rod through it, i.e. to skewer or transfix it.

clue.text: Coup leads to seizure by boss

parts.note: a master is a boss
a stroke is a sudden attack or seizure

explanation.surface: A political coup ends with the boss seizing power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coup' looks political, but it is the French word for a brilliant move.
explanation.definitionFit: A masterstroke is a brilliantly successful move, a stroke of genius.

clue.text: Pours from more than one side, one is told

indicators.note: one is told signals that the word is heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: sides in sport are teams, so several sides are teams

explanation.surface: Liquid spilling from several sides at once, so we hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pours' as in rain pouring down: it teems with rain.
explanation.definitionFit: When rain comes down in torrents it is said to teem, a synonym for pouring heavily.

clue.text: Fail to finish trap for insect

parts.note: to drag on is to go on and on, failing to finish
a trap and a fly are both light horse-drawn carriages

explanation.surface: A hunter fails to complete a snare meant for a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' reads as a snare for the insect, but it is a two-wheeled pony carriage, and a fly is another old hired carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The dragonfly is a large, long-bodied flying bug with two pairs of clear wings.

clue.text: Convincing demonstration that ridiculous person needs fewer clothes

parts.note: an object can be a person of ridiculous appearance, an object of mirth
wearing fewer clothes means having less on

explanation.surface: A clear proof that a comic figure ought to wear less.
explanation.definitionFit: An object lesson is a striking practical example that teaches or proves a point.

clue.text: Following out new order in anger

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the anger word

parts.note: to anger is to enrage

indicators.note: new order says the letters of out are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new regime emerging out of popular fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' reads as a noun but is the verb, to enrage; 'new order' and 'in' are the two signals, so 'out' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a group of attendants or supporters, a retinue.

clue.text: Plague that affected half of France in poem

indicators.note: in says the half word goes inside the poem

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem
demi is the French word for half

explanation.surface: A poem about a pestilence that struck half of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of France' tempts you to take half the letters of France, but it means the French word for half; 'that affected' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread outbreak of infectious disease.

clue.text: The doctor's English, the poet admits

indicators.note: admits says the poet's name lets the English letter inside

parts.note: A. E. Housman was the poet of A Shropshire Lad

explanation.surface: The poet concedes that the doctor is an Englishman.
explanation.walkthrough: A houseman is a British term for a junior hospital doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A houseman is a junior doctor resident in a British hospital, i.e. an intern.

clue.text: Sort of territory Cromwell gobbled up

parts.note: Oliver Cromwell ruled England as Lord Protector in the 1650s
gobbled up means ate

explanation.surface: A kind of land that Oliver Cromwell swallowed whole.
explanation.walkthrough: Cromwell's own period of rule is also called the Protectorate, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A protectorate is a state under the control and defence of a stronger power, one kind of dependent territory.

clue.text: A way to capture a snake on a ship

parts.note: a boa is a constricting snake
RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A road where someone catches a snake on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship or other vessel is being on board it.

clue.text: City man not so well-off?

explanation.surface: Is a financier really less rich than people think?
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; a City man works there.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockbroker is a City dealer; and comparing broke, someone with less money is more broke.

clue.text: To run away twice — not like this soldier

parts.note: to desert is to run away from duty
to rat is to abandon or run out on others

explanation.surface: A soldier who flees not once but twice; this one never did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not like this' adds irony: the Desert Rats, the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa in the Second World War, were famed for not running away.
explanation.definitionFit: A Desert Rat was a member of that armoured division, so a kind of soldier.

clue.text: Uplift revealed by bra is exciting

indicators.note: revealed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Support from a bra is a thrilling thing.
explanation.definitionFit: To uplift something is to elevate or lift it higher.

clue.text: Brown or black, there's uncertainty either way

parts.note: um is a hesitant noise showing uncertainty
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
er is another hesitant noise, placed on the other side

explanation.surface: Unsure whether the colour should be brown or black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either way' means on both sides: the two hesitation noises sit before and after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural earth pigment giving a dark brown colour.

clue.text: Account for former Israeli leader who called in the doctor

indicators.note: called in says the doctor is taken inside the leader's name

parts.note: Golda Meir was Prime Minister of Israel 1969-74
MO, medical officer, is a crossword doctor

explanation.surface: An explanation of why an ex-premier of Israel sent for a physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A memoir is a written account of one's own life and experiences.

clue.text: Cat with a cough — a fearsome hacker

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
to hawk is to clear the throat noisily, a sort of cough

explanation.surface: A cat with a hacking cough, sounding rather fierce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hacker' plays on the cough's hacking sound, but means a chopping tool, the North American war-axe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is a light axe used as a weapon, something that hacks fearsomely.

clue.text: The day the war-ended, rabbit was about as import

indicators.note: was about says the rabbit word surrounds the victory day

parts.note: a cony is a rabbit
VE Day, Victory in Europe, marked the end of the war in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: On VE Day, a rabbit seemed to be the bearer of significance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Import' is meaning or significance as a noun, used here as a verb sense: to convey meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To import, in the old sense, is to signify or carry a meaning, just as to convey is to communicate it.

clue.text: Back one who seeks to keep his title

definitions.text: one who seeks to keep his title

explanation.surface: A champion trying to hold on to his crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A full back in football guards the goal, and a reigning champion facing a challenger tries to retain the crown.
